intended_object: Vertical pasting of two 2-commutative squares of functors. Given an isomorphism H₁ ⋙ R₁ ≅ L₁ ⋙ H₂ and an isomorphism H₂ ⋙ R₂ ≅ L₂ ⋙ H₃, it gives the composite isomorphism H₁ ⋙ (R₁ ⋙ R₂) ≅ (L₁ ⋙ L₂) ⋙ H₃. I took this from the docstring, which calls it a variant of `vComp` ("Vertical composition of 2-commutative squares") where both squares are passed explicitly.
explanation:
The body turns the two explicit squares S₁ and S₂ into local instances and calls `vComp`, with the middle functor H₂ given explicitly. `vComp` builds the standard pasting isomorphism: H₁⋙(R₁⋙R₂) ≅ (H₁⋙R₁)⋙R₂ ≅ (L₁⋙H₂)⋙R₂ ≅ L₁⋙(H₂⋙R₂) ≅ L₁⋙(L₂⋙H₃) ≅ (L₁⋙L₂)⋙H₃. This is exactly the usual vertical composition of 2-commutative squares.

The categories and functors are arbitrary, so there is no generality issue. The definition only changes how the arguments are passed (explicit squares instead of instance arguments), so it agrees with `vComp`, which is the Mathlib declaration I cite as the counterpart.
